events.title: Guardium 驗證缺失漏洞
pts: 影響 IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2，**未經驗證的網路攻擊者可注入偽造稽核事件並存取監控原則**。
漏洞位於 SharePoint S-TAP RelayService（CVSS 9.1），無需驗證即可經網路觸發，目前尚未遭利用。

raw.desc: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to missing authentication in the SharePoint S-TAP RelayService, allowing an unauthenticated network attacker to inject forged audit events and access the active monitoring policy.

events.title: Splunk 遠端執行漏洞
pts: 影響 Splunk Enterprise、SOAR 與 Enterprise Security，**可致遠端執行程式碼或竄改資料**。
共 10 個 CVE（最高 CVSS 9.9），部分漏洞不需驗證即可觸發，目前尚未遭利用或勒索軟體攻擊。

descs:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the Apps edit, Containers edit, and Playbooks execute permissions could use the App Wizard to execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR. This could compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the Splunk SOAR instance.
The vulnerability exists because the App Wizard does not validate user-supplied identifiers before incorporating them into generated connector code.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Playbooks view, edit, execute, and delete permissions could cause existing cross-repository playbook references to run attacker-controlled playbook code.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR can bind existing cross-repository playbook references to a different source control repository when a deleted repository name is reused.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could use an empty clustering shared secret to read and modify clustering configuration through the cluster configuration Representational State Transfer (REST) API endpoint on a standalone instance. This could expose clustering configuration, persist attacker-controlled clustering settings, and disrupt clustering operations.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts the empty clustering shared secret as a shared-authentication candidate on a standalone instance when clustering is turned off.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_admin" Splunk Enterprise Security role could execute arbitrary code on the search head as the user account running Splunk Enterprise by combining lookup file upload and Configuration Checker functionality.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not restrict lookup upload file types or keep Configuration Checker module paths within the intended directory.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Create and manage lookups in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/managing-security-content/create-and-manage-lookups-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches through RapidDiag task collection as an authenticated user. With this access, the user could read or modify data and configuration available to that authenticated user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts an empty shared secret when it authenticates RapidDiag task-collection requests.
For more information see Using RapidDiag (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/troubleshoot/9.3/contact-splunk-support/using-rapiddiag) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_investigation_read capability could cause the Risk Event Timeline Representational State Transfer (REST) API to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could expose stored credentials and modify indexes and lookup data available to those permissions.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected REST API does not validate request values before including them in search macro arguments.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Risk analysis (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/risk-analysis) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user who can influence indexed event data could store attacker-controlled values in event fields. If another authenticated user who reviews the event selects the View Adaptive Response Invocations or View Adaptive Response Results workflow action from Event Actions, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the action. The unauthenticated user could then access or modify sensitive data and disrupt services available to the user who selects the action.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected Common Information Model workflow actions insert the orig_sid and orig_rid event-field values directly into searches without safely validating or quoting the values.
For more information see About workflow actions in Splunk Web (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.2/workflow-actions/about-workflow-actions-in-splunk-web) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with edit permission for the container label on a pending approval could read an external-prompt capability through an Approval details Representational State Transfer (REST) API response and use it to view the prompt content, change the pending approval decision, and modify its action parameters.
The vulnerability is possible because an Approval details response exposes the external-prompt capability without checking approval ownership.
For more information see REST External Prompt (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.5.0/external-prompt-endpoints/rest-external-prompt) and Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.5.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Assets edit or delete permission and access to one or more tenants could change or delete assets assigned to other tenants through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. With this access, the user could redirect connector traffic and expose the credentials and operational data associated with an asset, or disrupt integrations and data ingestion for other tenants.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR verifies the Assets edit or delete permission but does not verify that the user can access every tenant assigned to the target asset before Splunk SOAR changes or deletes the asset.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance), Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.6.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), and Using the REST API reference for Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.5.0/using-the-splunk-soar-rest-api/using-the-rest-api-reference-for-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR by installing a malicious app.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not restrict app dependencies to validated binary packages before installing them.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with only the apps:edit permission could install a connector app that causes Splunk SOAR to write attacker-controlled files outside the app directory. This could let the user modify files used by Splunk SOAR and execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR constructs the dependency installation command from app-supplied metadata without preventing that metadata from changing its arguments.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.6.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could cause Splunk SOAR to execute arbitrary code on the host when the user validates an installed app.
The vulnerability is possible because the app validation workflow does not isolate untrusted code from the trusted environment.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with repository edit access could cause Splunk SOAR to write files outside the configured repository, which lets the user modify files that the user account running Splunk SOAR can write to.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not require source control repository paths to remain inside the configured repository.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view and edit containers for one label could use a slash command through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API to access sensitive product data and credentials outside the authorized container scope.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not enforce authorization for related objects that slash commands access from an authorized artifact.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to create and run playbooks could start child playbooks on containers outside the authorized label, or repository scope for that user. This could expose container data and affect automation outside that scope.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not bind the identity used to authorize the child playbook run to the parent playbook execution context.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could cause Splunk Enterprise to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with elevated privileges through data model acceleration.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly neutralize caller-supplied data model acceleration values before it places them into generated summarization searches.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 9.4.17, 10.0.12, 10.2.9, and 10.4.5, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles can configure a metric alert through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API that runs a search with elevated privileges. The vulnerability lets the user access or modify data and disrupt the Splunk Enterprise instance.
The vulnerability occurs because Splunk Enterprise does not enforce the required role-based authorization when it processes metric alert configuration through the REST API. Splunk Enterprise schedules the resulting search with elevated authorization and runs attacker-controlled search processing with that authorization.
For more information see About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for a container or workbook task could store attacker-controlled Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) in a note. When another user with view permission for the affected container and its notes opens the affected note in Mission Control, the note could run unauthorized JavaScript code in the browser of that user, expose data available through the authenticated session, and perform actions available through the authenticated session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not neutralize active content in all notes before Mission Control renders them.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with the containers:edit permission could import a container that includes a malicious Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) note. When another user views the imported note, Splunk SOAR could run unauthorized JavaScript in the browser of that user, exposing data and allowing actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not sanitize HTML note content during container import before it renders the content in Mission Control.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could modify a search macro associated with risk exclusions. Scheduled Risk data model acceleration searches could later run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands from that macro with elevated permissions. With this access, the user who modified the search macro could expose stored credentials and modify indexes or lookup data available to those searches.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk Enterprise Security app metadata grants the "ess_analyst" role write access to the risk exclusion search macro.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.3/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security), and Use search macros in searches (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/search-macros/use-search-macros-in-searches) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the ueba_ers_execution_post capability could cause the User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Content App to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions through an Entity Risk Score calculation. With this access, the user could expose stored credentials and other data outside the permissions assigned to that role.
The vulnerability is possible because the UEBA Content App does not validate Entity Risk Score calculation values before including them in SPL searches.
For more information see Installing the UEBA Content App for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.5/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/installing-the-ueba-content-app-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Entity risk scoring in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.4/risk-based-alerting/entity-risk-scoring-in-splunk-enterprise-security), and Roles and knowledge objects in UEBA for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.8/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/ueba-content-app-for-on-premises/roles-and-knowledge-objects-in-ueba-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the ueba_finding_exclusion_edit capability could store attacker-controlled values in a User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) finding exclusion rule. Splunk Enterprise Security could later run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands from the rule with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could cause Splunk Enterprise Security to read stored credentials and modify lookups and knowledge objects.
The vulnerability is possible because the UEBA finding exclusion workflow does not escape user-controlled rule values before using them in generated SPL.
For more information see Create a finding exclusion rule using UEBA configuration page (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security/create-a-finding-exclusion-rule-using-ueba-configuration-page) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_investigation_read capability could inject arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) into Mission Control dashboard search requests. Mission Control could then run the injected SPL with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could cause Mission Control to read stored credentials and write data to indexes and lookups.
The vulnerability is possible because Mission Control does not validate reserved search filters before adding them to dashboard searches.
For more information see Overview of Mission Control in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.1/mission-control/overview-of-mission-control-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.2/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit and run playbooks could read or overwrite persisted data for playbook runs outside the authorized label, or ownership scope for that user. The affected data can include playbook inputs, prompt and block results, outputs, and secrets that playbooks save in run data. Overwriting the data could corrupt results that paused, scheduled, or parent playbook runs later use.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook automation APIs do not bind data operations to the active playbook run.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could create an attacker-controlled saved search. Threat intelligence lookup generation could later run the saved search with elevated permissions, which could let the user who created the saved search run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with those permissions.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not restrict threat intelligence lookup generation to the intended saved searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Turn on threat matching searches in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.0/threat-intelligence/turn-on-threat-matching-searches-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the ueba_finding_exclusion_edit capability could create a finding exclusion rule that references an attacker-controlled lookup definition if the role also grants write access to globally shared lookup definitions, as the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role does. The User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Content App could later include the lookup name in a search and run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user who created the finding exclusion rule could expose stored credentials and other data outside the permissions assigned to the "ess_analyst" role.
The vulnerability is possible because UEBA finding exclusion processing does not safely quote lookup names before including them in SPL searches.
For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.3/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Roles and knowledge objects in UEBA for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.8/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/ueba-content-app-for-on-premises/roles-and-knowledge-objects-in-ueba-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who holds the "Observer" Splunk SOAR role could access a password-reset credential in a diagnostic log bundle and reset the password for an active local account.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not redact password-reset email bodies before it logs communications between product processes.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an operator of a configured identity provider could authenticate as an existing user associated with another configured identity provider. If that account has the "Administrator" Splunk SOAR role, the operator could control the Splunk SOAR deployment.
Splunk SOAR does not bind external user accounts to the identity provider that provisions them and authenticates accounts by username without verifying provider ownership.
The vulnerability requires more than one configured external identity provider with distinct trust domains and a target username that an operator of a configured identity provider can authenticate through a different provider.
For more information see Configure single sign-on authentication (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/configure-single-sign-on-authentication-for-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Manage roles and permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0 a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could access data associated with another tenant and cause actions to be attributed to that tenant through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk AI Assistant accepted a client-controlled tenant identifier when selecting the authorization context for a request.

In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could submit client-controlled feature settings through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could modify limited response metadata outside the expected server-side configuration.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API processes client-supplied feature settings without enforcing the expected server-side configuration boundary.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could cause scheduled metric alert searches to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and access credentials stored in cleartext. This requires at least one non-internal metric index on the instance.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not fully validate metric alert filter input before using it in a scheduled search.

events.title: Fastify 外掛路徑穿越漏洞
pts: 影響 @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4 前版本，搭 Tomcat 等後端可繞過路徑存取內部 API。
尚未遭利用；未經身分驗證者可發送含分號路徑參數請求利用，nginx 不受影響。
events.fix: **升級 @fastify/reply-from 至 12.8.4 以上版本**

raw.desc: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

events.title: SQL Server 漏洞 CVE-2026-87867
pts: MRemoteNG establishes encrypted but unauthenticated channel with Microsoft SQL Server backend. Client accepts any certificate the server pre

raw.desc:
MRemoteNG establishes encrypted but unauthenticated channel with Microsoft SQL Server backend. Client accepts any certificate the server
presents, including a self-signed certificate supplied by an attacker. An attacker positioned between the client and the SQL server (for example via ARP/DNS spoofing) can
transparently pintercept the connection (man-in-the-middle) and read all traffic, including the encrypted connection-password table read and the database login.




Vendor did not provide the range of vulnerable versions. Only version 1.76.20 was tested and confirmed vulnerable. Other versions may also be vulnerable.

events.title: vCenter 驗證繞過漏洞
pts: 影響 vCenter 及 Telco Cloud，**VMware Directory Service 存在驗證繞過漏洞**。
CVSS 為 9.8，影響 vCenter 5.x/8.0/9.0.x/9.1.x 等產品，目前尚未發現遭利用。

raw.desc:
VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service.
Affected versions: 9.1.x (fixed in 9.1.1.0200); 9.0.x (fixed in 9.0.2.0200); 8.0 (fixed in 8.0 U3m); 5.x (fixed in 5.2.5).
Telco Cloud Platform 3.0, 4.x, 5.0.x, 5.1.x, 5.2 and Telco Cloud Infrastructure 3.0 are also affected (see KB463116).

events.title: PHP 遠端執行與提權漏洞
pts: 影響 PHP Session、PHP-FPM 與 HTTP 串流等元件，**可導致遠端執行程式碼、權限提升或阻斷服務**。
共 9 個 CVE（最高 CVSS 9.2），包含多起釋放後使用（UAF）漏洞，目前尚未發現遭利用。

descs:
Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.

Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown.

A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution.

When collecting the arguments of a method call handled by __call() or __callStatic() for a backtrace, PHP can read stale values that may refer to freed memory. If a fatal error such as exceeding memory_limit occurs while an application enters such a call, with fatal_error_backtraces enabled (the default) and zend.exception_ignore_args disabled, a remote attacker who controls enough request data to influence memory allocation may cause memory corruption, crash the PHP worker or, with knowledge of memory addresses, execute arbitrary code. php.ini-production enables zend.exception_ignore_args, which prevents this.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown.

The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an application callback while the session variables are destroyed at shutdown, such as stream_close() of a user-defined stream wrapper, the pointer is retained after the request memory is freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can free the stale string. An attacker who can trigger such a failing cleanup may crash the worker or corrupt memory; code execution has not been demonstrated. This requires the filename to be allocated in request memory, for example when the script is not cached by OPcache.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.

In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

events.title: AI 平台存取與路徑漏洞
pts: 影響 Dialoqbase、Zyrabit Platform 與 SGLang，**存在路徑穿越及授權缺失風險**。
共 3 個 CVE（最高 CVSS 9.8），部分端點不需驗證即可透過網路存取，目前尚未遭利用。
events.fix: Dialoqbase 升至 1.11.5、Zyrabit Platform 升至 2.4.4，SGLang 套用 commit 7b5fb39

descs: Dialoqbase is an application for creating chatbots. Prior to 1.11.5, the unauthenticated GET /api/v1/view/* route in server/src/routes/api/v1/view/root.ts resolves its attacker-controlled wildcard path without normalization or containment, allowing traversal outside the intended uploads directory and arbitrary server file reads. Reading environment files can disclose DB_SECRET_KEY, the application’s JWT signing key, which permits forged administrator tokens and takeover of bots, conversations, integrations, and stored third-party credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.5.

Zyrabit Platform provides sovereign AI infrastructure for enterprise retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 2.4.4, import_to_vault(source_path, destination_name) accepts both caller-controlled paths, but the content-pattern guard does not confine destination_name. The vulnerable tool is implemented in zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/domain/services/mcp_service.py, where Path(DOCS_DIR) / destination_name is passed to shutil.copy2, allowing traversal or an absolute destination to write outside the vault. An unrestricted source_path can be copied into the vault and retrieved through secure_query, disclosing files readable by the service; files that do not match the executable-pattern filter pass that filter. When ENABLE_LEGACY_EXTENSIONS=true, zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/main.py registers POST /mcp/rpc without get_current_user, allowing unauthenticated network tool calls; this optional exposure is disabled by default and is not required for local invocation. If an attacker can stage chosen source content and write to an execution-triggered destination, the advisory describes conditional process execution. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.4.

SGLang through 0.5.23, fixed in commit 7b5fb39, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the POST /load_lora_adapter_from_tensors HTTP endpoint, which lacks the @auth_level(AuthLevel.ADMIN_OPTIONAL) decorator applied to its sibling admin endpoints, allowing unauthenticated network-reachable attackers to invoke it without an API key. Attackers can load a LoRA adapter from attacker-supplied serialized tensors to manipulate the served model, and when combined with a separately documented deserialization bypass, achieve unauthenticated remote code execution as root.

events.title: NGINX 遠端執行與阻斷漏洞
pts: 影響 NGINX Plus 與 Open Source（HTTP/2、HTTP/3、郵件代理等），**可致執行程式碼或阻斷服務**。
共 8 個 CVE（最高 CVSS 9.2），多數需特定組態或條件（如未啟用 ASLR、TLSv1.3），目前尚未遭利用。

descs:
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

events.title: Ivanti 遠端執行漏洞
pts: 影響 Airlock Gateway 8.5.2 及更早版本與 8.6.0，**可導致阻斷服務或遠端執行程式碼**。
目前尚未遭利用；須啟用 Smart Form Protection 且後端回傳含特定多位元組 HTML 字元參照時觸發。
events.fix: 升級至 Airlock Gateway 8.5.3 或 8.6.1 版本。

raw.desc:
A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0)  allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart Form Protection feature, possibly leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or Remote Code Execution (RCE) attack against the Airlock Gateway. The issue has been fixed in Airlock Gateway version 8.5.3 and 8.6.1.

For an attack to be executable, the Airlock Gateway needs to have 'Smart Form Protection' (or the corresponding expert settings) enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references. The buffer overflow then happens during the parsing of that HTML response. Such a response can come either from a malicious or compromised backend, or from an otherwise trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, e.g. an application that stores and serves plain user-provided HTML files.

Successfully exploiting the vulnerability can enable an attacker to perform a DoS attack or, in the worst case, an RCE attack against the Airlock Gateway in front of the affected backend. Compromising the functionality of the Airlock Gateway could in this way also affect the availability and protection of other well-intentioned backends deployed behind the same Gateway.

events.title: Linux 核心多項漏洞
pts: 影響 Linux 核心 KVM x86 與 logitech-hidpp 驅動，涉及 MMU 重設與競爭條件問題。
尚未遭利用；**最高 CVSS 8.8，上游核心程式碼已修復該兩項問題**。

descs:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer

The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated
buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync).
However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns.

If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the
send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has
updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will
observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer.

This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel
stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command).

Fix this by:
1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex
   in the synchronous command path.
2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers
   inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding
   a NULL check before dereferencing.

events.title: Synology 遠端執行漏洞
pts: 影響 Synology DSM 與 BeeStation OS (BSM) 系統外掛常駐程式，遠端攻擊者可藉此執行任意程式碼。
**此漏洞已遭實際利用**，無勒索軟體利用紀錄；屬輸出編碼或跳脫不當漏洞，可透過未明途徑觸發。

pts: 影響 Apache Axis（可能已終止支援 EoL/EoS），未經身分驗證的遠端攻擊者可執行任意程式碼。
**此漏洞已遭實際利用**，無勒索軟體利用紀錄；當 classpath 存在適用類別時，可透過特製 SOAP 錯誤訊息觸發。
events.fix: 依原廠公告套用修補或緩解措施；受影響版本可能已終止支援，建議停用或轉換至受支援版本。

raw.name: Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
raw.desc: Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted SOAP fault message that causes Axis to load and instantiate an attacker-specified class when a suitable class is available on the application classpath. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

events.title: Chrome 多項遠端執行漏洞
pts: 影響 Windows 版 Google Chrome 158.0.8127.36 前版本，**可於沙盒外遠端執行程式碼**。
尚未遭利用；需透過特製 HTML 網頁觸發，部分漏洞須配合社交工程或已入侵算繪程序。

descs: Use after free in Accessibility in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Use after free in Omnibox in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Incorrect authorization in Omnibox in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process and leveraged social engineering to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Race condition in Downloads in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process and leveraged social engineering to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Use after free in CameraCapture in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker leveraging social engineering to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Use after free in Mojo in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Use after free in Mojo in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

events.title: AI 平台驗證繞過與阻斷漏洞
pts: 影響 BISHENG 3.0.0 前、53AIHub 0.5.5 前及 vLLM，**可致未授權取得管理權限或服務中斷**。
目前尚未發現遭利用；攻擊者可遠端無需驗證偽造權杖、重設帳戶或透過特定請求癱瘓系統。

descs: BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to impersonate administrators by abusing a hard-coded default jwt_secret used by AuthJwt. Attackers can forge an HS256 token offline naming user_id 1 with the admin role, send it as access_token_cookie, and gain full administrative access to users, workspaces, knowledge bases and workflows.

53AIHub before 0.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to reinitialize installed instances by calling the public POST /api/init endpoint. Attackers can reset an existing account's password, assign the top creator role, and obtain an access token to take over accounts and use admin-only API routes.

vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range prompt token ids when served with --skip-tokenizer-init. Attackers can submit a large positive token id to /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, or /pooling, bypassing the tokenizer-gated vocab check and causing a fatal embedding index error that denies service to all tenants.

vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one request. Attackers can send a compact request to /v1/messages or /v1/responses that forces downloading and decoding of every image before prompt-length admission, exhausting memory, CPU, and connections.

BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to impersonate administrators by abusing a hard-coded default jwt_secret used by AuthJwt. Attackers can forge an HS256 token offline naming user_id 1 with the admin role, send it as access_token_cookie, and gain full administrative access to users, workspaces, knowledge bases and workflows.

53AIHub before 0.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to reinitialize installed instances by calling the public POST /api/init endpoint. Attackers can reset an existing account's password, assign the top creator role, and obtain an access token to take over accounts and use admin-only API routes.

vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range prompt token ids when served with --skip-tokenizer-init. Attackers can submit a large positive token id to /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, or /pooling, bypassing the tokenizer-gated vocab check and causing a fatal embedding index error that denies service to all tenants.

vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one request. Attackers can send a compact request to /v1/messages or /v1/responses that forces downloading and decoding of every image before prompt-length admission, exhausting memory, CPU, and connections.

Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264, the routes for PluginService::regenerateSecret and PluginService::delete carry no @Permissions decorator, and the methods omit plugin ownership checks. An authenticated attacker can directly target another plugin's identifier to rotate and disclose its OAuth secret or delete the plugin, including system plugins. Separately, PermissionGuard authorizes several nested API requests using a caller-controlled parent tableId, baseId, or spaceId, while the services resolve the requested child object only by its globally unique identifier. An authenticated attacker can provide a parent resource the attacker owns together with a victim's child identifier. ViewService::getViewById can then disclose another tenant's view configuration, embedded filter values, field layout, and shareId. DashboardService::updatePluginStorage and the view-position updatePluginStorage path can overwrite another tenant's plugin storage because the plugin installation is not rebound to the authorized base, dashboard, table, or view. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264.

Flowise 3.1.3 through 3.1.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read MCP server bearer tokens via the GET /api/v1/public-chatflows/:id handler. Attackers can use the leaked mcpServerConfig token on the POST /api/v1/mcp/:chatflowId route to invoke chatflows, bypassing API key protection and consuming the owner's model quota.

Atlassian recommends that Bamboo Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:

events.title: GitLab 指令碼與存取漏洞
pts: 影響 GitLab CE/EE 9.3 起未修補版本，**已驗證使用者可執行任意 JavaScript 或存取受保護 CI/CD 資源**。
包含 3 項 CVE，最高 CVSS 8.7，目前尚未遭利用，亦無勒索軟體利用紀錄，須登入且符合特定條件才會觸發。
events.fix: 升級 GitLab CE/EE 至 19.3.9、19.4.8 或 19.5.6 以上版本。

descs: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of users viewing a wiki page due to improper sanitization of user input.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 16.1 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of users viewing Error Tracking pages due to improper sanitization of user input.

raw.name: Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
raw.desc: Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet’s report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.
raw.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

events.title: Phoenix 與 53AIHub 漏洞
pts: 影響 Phoenix 13.0.0 至 15.7.0 及 53AIHub 0.5.5 前版本，**可致未授權讀取知識庫檔案與屬性遍歷**。
目前尚無遭利用紀錄；攻擊者無需驗證即可列舉數字 ID 竊取檔案，或透過惡意模板字串攻擊。

descs: Phoenix is an AI observability and evaluation platform. From 13.0.0 until 15.7.0, the applyChatTemplate GraphQL query passed attacker-controlled F-string templates to FStringTemplateFormatter._format, while DotDict.__getattr__ did not prevent traversal through Python private attributes. A crafted field could traverse object internals such as __class__, __init__, and __globals__ to read process environment variables and internal module state. The endpoint is unauthenticated on default installations, and any account can reach it when authentication is enabled. Exposure of PHOENIX_SECRET can allow administrative session-token forgery and decryption of credentials protected by keys derived from that secret. This issue is fixed in version 15.7.0.

53AIHub before 0.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files by requesting /api/files/:file_id/preview and /api/file-version/:file_body_id without UserTokenAuth. Attackers can enumerate sequential numeric ids to read raw knowledge-base files and stored file versions belonging to any enterprise tenant.

events.title: DeepAudit 洩密漏洞
pts: 影響 DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 至 3.8.0，**未登入攻擊者可取得 LLM 金鑰與 GitLab 等權杖**。
另有 SSRF 漏洞供註冊使用者外洩伺服器端權杖；目前尚未遭利用或用於勒索軟體，CVSS 8.7。

descs: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve server secrets through the /api/v1/config/defaults endpoint. Attackers can send a GET request to obtain the operator's LLM provider API keys and GitHub or GitLab tokens, then abuse those services and accessible repositories.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows registered users to leak server-wide GitLab or Gitea tokens via repository_url. Attackers can create a gitlab or gitea project pointing to a controlled host and request its branches to capture the operator's token and reach internal hosts.

events.title: OpenSSL 搜尋路徑漏洞
pts: 影響 Netskope Client 與 Endpoint DLP 內嵌 OpenSSL，**可致 SYSTEM 權限執行程式碼**。
僅影響 Windows，尚未傳出遭利用，需本機已驗證攻擊者在次要磁碟建立惡意設定檔，macOS 與 Linux 不受影響。

raw.desc: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

events.title: Linux 核心多項記憶體漏洞
pts: 影響 Linux 核心 ceph、nfsd、ksmbd 及 smb 元件，**存在整數溢位、釋放後使用與越界寫入風險**。
目前尚無遭利用紀錄；相關漏洞涉及檔案系統與 SMB 處理流程，部分問題已在核心中修正。

descs:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check

ceph_update_snap_trace() bounds the two encoded snapid arrays that follow a
struct ceph_mds_snap_realm with sizeof(u64) * (num_snaps +
num_prior_parent_snaps).  Both counts come straight off the wire as __le32,
so the addition is evaluated in unsigned int and wraps before sizeof(u64)
promotes it to size_t: an MDS sending num_snaps = 1 and
num_prior_parent_snaps = 0xffffffff makes the sum zero and the check
degenerates to ceph_decode_need(&p, e, 0, bad), which always passes.
dup_array() then reads num_snaps * 8 bytes past the end of the message
front, which ceph_msg_new2() allocates at exactly front_len bytes.  An
unsolicited CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_SNAP reaches this from a malicious or
compromised MDS with no client-side action, as do the snaptraces carried in
an MDS reply and in a cap import.

Compute the length with size_add()/size_mul() so it saturates at SIZE_MAX
instead of wrapping, in the style fs/ceph/mdsmap.c already uses for
num_export_targets.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in dup_array (include/linux/unaligned.h:28 fs/ceph/snap.c:500)
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880102a16c8 by task kworker/1:2/129
  Workqueue: ceph-msgr ceph_con_workfn
  Call Trace:
   dump_stack_lvl (lib/dump_stack.c:94 lib/dump_stack.c:120)
   print_report (mm/kasan/report.c:378 mm/kasan/report.c:482)
   kasan_report (mm/kasan/report.c:595)
   dup_array (include/linux/unaligned.h:28 fs/ceph/snap.c:500)
   ceph_update_snap_trace (fs/ceph/snap.c:836)
   ceph_handle_snap (fs/ceph/snap.c:1155)
   mds_dispatch (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:7234)
   ceph_con_process_message (net/ceph/messenger.c:1424)
   ceph_con_v1_try_read (net/ceph/messenger_v1.c:1430)
   ceph_con_workfn (net/ceph/messenger.c:1576)
   process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3396)
   worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3479 kernel/workqueue.c:3560)
   kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)
   ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:158)
   ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245)
  ...
  The buggy address is located 0 bytes to the right of
   allocated 72-byte region [ffff8880102a1680, ffff8880102a16c8)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks

check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks
it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire:
ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then
overwrites it with the size of the "in" set.  Neither is bounded by
CEPH_MAX_MDS, only by m_info allocating, so a monitor announcing more ranks
than the bitmap holds makes test_bit() read past the end of targets[].  The
clear_bit() loop above indexes the same bitmap, though it is additionally
bounded by mdsc->max_sessions.  The map arrives on the monitor connection,
which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode.

CEPH_MAX_MDS is a protocol constant from src/mds/mdstypes.h, and the
reserved inode ranges in super.h are laid out one rank apart over that
span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt.  Reject it where the rank
space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map().

  BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in check_new_map (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:5968)
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffc90000ac7798 by task kworker/1:2/127
  Workqueue: ceph-msgr ceph_con_workfn
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   dump_stack_lvl (lib/dump_stack.c:94 lib/dump_stack.c:120)
   print_report (mm/kasan/report.c:378 mm/kasan/report.c:482)
   kasan_report (mm/kasan/report.c:595)
   kasan_check_range (mm/kasan/generic.c:186 mm/kasan/generic.c:200)
   check_new_map (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:5968)
   ceph_mdsc_handle_mdsmap (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:7060)
   extra_mon_dispatch (fs/ceph/super.c:802)
   mon_dispatch (net/ceph/mon_client.c:1483)
   ceph_con_process_message (net/ceph/messenger.c:1424)
   ceph_con_v1_try_read (net/ceph/messenger_v1.c:1430)
   ceph_con_workfn (net/ceph/messenger.c:1576)
   process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3396)
   worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3479 kernel/workqueue.c:3560)
   kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids
without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under
cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched
creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner.

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140
  fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners()
  nfsd4_exchange_id
  nfsd4_proc_compound
  nfsd_dispatch
  svc_process

Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner
list.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix app-instance non-durable supersede session UAF

ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id() supersedes a prior open that has the
same AppInstanceId. It reaches that open's session through opinfo->sess.
This pointer is not refcounted.

Session teardown detaches durable handles before it frees the session.
It does not detach a non-durable open. That open still points at the
session through opinfo->sess after the session is freed. Another session
can supersede the open at the same time. The supersede then takes a
write lock through the stale pointer, in the freed session's file table.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
  Call Trace:
   _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
   ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id+0xd9/0x670 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x3e10/0xd910 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 212:
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0x38d/0x480 [ksmbd]

Fix this by looking the session up by opinfo->session_id. The lookup
returns a reference, as smb2_break_collect_channels() does. Recheck that
opinfo->sess still points at it before using it.

Do the lookup without m_lock held. destroy_previous_session() takes
m_lock under the session table lock, and taking them in the other order
here would deadlock.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix SMB2 CREATE response buffer overflow

smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() uses the MAX_CIFS_SMALL_BUFFER_SIZE
(448-byte) buffer for a single SMB2_CREATE response. That buffer also
holds a 4-byte length field, which only leaves 444 bytes for the SMB2
body.

The AAPL response made this buffer too small. After 8f1b796ff113, a
request with AAPL response contexts may need at least 456 bytes. In
the 456-byte case, create_aapl_rsp_buf() is appended last, clears 128
bytes, and writes 12 bytes past the allocation.

KASAN reports:

    BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    Write of size 128 at addr ffff88800370954c by task kworker/0:0/9
    ...
    create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    smb2_open+0x58f9/0xef10
    ...
    smb2_allocate_rsp_buf+0x19d/0x370
    ...
    The buggy address is located 332 bytes inside of
     allocated 448-byte region [ffff888003709400, ffff8880037095c0)

Reserve enough space for any fixed CREATE response KSMBD can build.
Store the required allocation size in the per-dialect values table.
This keeps the small buffer for other commands and avoids using the max
transaction buffer for every CREATE.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()

In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after
commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group
rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or
5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace)
on posix).

However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() ->
copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total),
and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes)
even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security
descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or
dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past
the end of the slab buffer.

Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of
id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()

When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct
smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed,
Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This
only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So
the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd.

    unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset);
    int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset;

    if (!dacl_offset ||
	(dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size))
	    goto out;

Commit beff0bc9d69b ("ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check")
fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out,
because it is only valid for 32-bit builds.

Reproduced on 32-bit ARM with KASAN, by a client sending SMB2
SET_INFO(SEC) with dacloffset=0xfffffff8, then QUERY_INFO(SEC) on the
same file:

 BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105)
 Read of size 2 at addr c2a273fa by task kworker/1:1/35
 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 35 Comm: kworker/1:1 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc2+ #5
 Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
 Call trace:
  kasan_check_range from build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105)
  build_sec_desc from smb2_query_info (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:7676)
  smb2_query_info from handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:160)
  handle_ksmbd_work from process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3401)
  process_one_work from worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3473)
  worker_thread from kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)

Add overflow check.

events.title: GitLab 等分支保護繞過
pts: 影響 Atlassian 與 GitLab 分支保護規則，**具寫入權限者可繞過保護修改檔案或新增執行工作流程**。
此漏洞（CVE-2026-123638）CVSS 8.3，須具備儲存庫寫入權限，目前尚未遭利用或用於勒索軟體。

raw.desc: The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path.

events.title: nginx 反向代理未驗證漏洞
pts: 影響依文件設 Nginx 反向代理的 Hugo Blog（commit 744ca15 及以前），**未驗證者可濫用 API 金鑰**。
尚未傳出遭利用，遠端免驗證即可發動攻擊，造成 API 配額與費用耗盡及服務中斷。

raw.desc: Hugo Blog is a tech blog site. In commit 744ca15 and prior, the AI assistant proxy exposes three HTTP endpoints (POST /api/blog-assistant, POST /api/blog-search-embedding, POST /api/blog-search-rerank) without any authentication check. When deployed following the documented Nginx reverse-proxy setup, any unauthenticated remote attacker can send arbitrary requests that the proxy forwards to the upstream LLM/embedding/rerank API using the operator's server-side API key (OPENAI_API_KEY / AI_SEARCH_API_KEY). This enables unlimited quota consumption, cost exhaustion, and potential service unavailability for the operator. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches.

events.title: vLLM 阻斷服務漏洞
pts: 影響 vLLM 0.10.1 至 0.31.0 前受影響版本，**遠端攻擊者可藉特定請求使引擎崩潰或造成 CPU 過度負荷**。
包含 2 項 CVE，最高 CVSS 8.7，目前尚未遭利用，亦無勒索軟體利用紀錄，影響 XD-RoPE 與 Cohere2 Vision 模型處理。

descs: vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.30.0 contains a reachable assertion vulnerability in GPUModelRunner._init_xdrope_positions that allows remote attackers to crash the engine by submitting embeddings-only requests. Attackers can send a /v1/completions request containing only prompt_embeds to XD-RoPE models with --enable-prompt-embeds, terminating the EngineCore and API server for all clients.

vLLM from 0.10.1 before 0.31.0 forwards a request-controlled mm_processor_kwargs.max_patches value to the Hugging Face processor for Cohere2 Vision models without a server-side upper bound, causing quadratic CPU work during multimodal preprocessing. Remote clients can send small image chat-completion requests with large, varying max_patches values to bypass the LRU cache, exhaust preprocessing workers, and deny service to other clients.

raw.desc: 一場網路攻擊，從取得受害系統的存取權限，到透過多個AI Agent協同執行攻擊，最後大規模蒐集存取憑證，可能不到六小時就能完成。攻擊者不再只是逐步尋找漏洞、手動執行攻擊，而是利用AI串聯不同階段的工作，在短時間內擴大攻擊規模。 Google威脅情報小組（Google Threat Intelligence Group，GTIG）技術長Shane Huntley指出，AI並未從根本上改變網路攻擊的本質，卻讓攻擊者能以更快的速度、更大的規模執行既有攻擊。過去受限於人力與時間，攻擊者必須選擇目標；如今AI可以協助搜尋漏洞、分析系統及執行攻擊，企業原本認為風險不高的弱點，也可能成為入侵入口。

events.title: Telerik UI 解析漏洞
pts: Telerik UI for ASP.NET MVC 2012.2.710–2026.3.1015 與 Core 2015.1.318–2026.3.1015 **伺服器端篩選解析與輸入驗證存有缺陷**。
涵蓋 CVE-2026-106146、CVE-2026-106154（CVSS 8.6），目前尚未遭利用，涉及未經驗證之篩選參數處理。

descs: In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET MVC versions `2012.2.710` through `2026.3.1015`, server-side filter processing does not properly validate descriptor types, null values, or stack state in FilterNodeVisitor and does not catch FilterParserException within the affected assembly. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an endpoint reachable without authentication that accepts crafted filter parameters. Affected requests can trigger uncaught cast, null-reference, or empty-stack exceptions and return HTTP 500. The report does not demonstrate worker-process termination or disruption of unrelated requests. The issue is fixed in version `2026.4.1111`.

In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET Core versions `2015.1.318` through `2026.3.1015`, the server-side FilterParser processes nested expressions in untrusted filter parameters through recursive parsing without a recursion-depth limit, while FilterLexer does not enforce an input-length limit. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an endpoint using DataSourceRequest model binding that is reachable without authentication. Deeply nested filters can trigger parsing errors during model binding or cause `StackOverflowException`. This issue is fixed in version `2026.4.1111`.
